messages:
Alex: Hey team, EdgeCtl (acct edge-772) is seeing a burst of 429s every minute or so. Customer says it looks like RPM/TPM limit hits, but traffic is fairly steady. Sample from their logs:

```
2026-03-15T14:12:00Z POST /api/v1/generate 429 "rate limit exceeded" user=edge-772 tokens=120
2026-03-15T14:12:01Z POST /api/v1/generate 200 tokens=89
2026-03-15T14:13:00Z POST /api/v1/generate 429 "rate limit exceeded" user=edge-772 tokens=130
```

Alex: They also shared a curl trace with headers:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-edge-xxxx" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
< HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
< Retry-After: 1
< X-RateLimit-RPM: 600
< X-RateLimit-TPM: 150
```

Maria: Thanks Alex. Can you drop the customer request id and the org id? I'll pull their quota config. Also, are they using many concurrent connections or streaming?

Alex: Org id is org_042-edge. They reported ~12 concurrent connections from one host, mostly short requests (50-150 tokens). Not streaming.

Jay: Paging in SRE. Quick hypothesis: request bursts aligning with minute boundary causing token refill/rolling-window mismatch. Could be client retries + concurrent short requests producing a peak at second 00.

Anna: Two things to check: 1) token bucket config for org_042-edge (rpm/ tpm windows), 2) proxy layer (customer using our edge-proxy or their own?). If they use a proxy that batches/replays at 1-minute marks that explains spikes.

Alex: They're on our edge-proxy (edgectl) with default connection pool. Customer says they do a fanout to 12 workers on a cron tick every minute.

Maria: OK that is the smoking gun. Cron + fanout -> minute alignment. Suggested immediate mitigation: advise customer to jitter cron, add small randomized delay (100-500ms) between worker requests, or enable per-worker stagger. I can ask for logs showing timestamps to confirm alignment.

Jay: From our side we can temporarily raise RPM for org_042-edge by 20% for 1 hour while they rollout jitter. To check current usage pattern run this query in monitoring:
```
SELECT count(*) as reqs, date_trunc('second', ts) as t
FROM api.requests
WHERE org_id='org_042-edge' AND ts > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY t
ORDER BY t DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

Anna: Also check our ratecap metrics: token_refill_jitter, bucket_occupancy, and proxy-backpressure drops. If occupancy hits 100% exactly at :00 it's definitely alignment.

Alex: Customer just pasted a short sample showing dense requests at :00 and :01. I'll attach and ask them to try jitter.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-284 created and linked to this thread. Assigned to Maria and Jay. ETA for initial response: 30m. :white_check_mark:

Maria: Action items: 1) Alex - collect a 5-minute pcap/trace showing per-second counts. 2) Jay - run the monitoring query and check bucket occupancy. 3) Anna - prepare a temporary quota bump playbook (so we can flip on +20% quickly). I'll message customer with recommended jitter and backoff settings: use exponential backoff with base 100ms and cap 1s, and add random jitter 0-200ms between fanout requests.

Jay: If we see client-side retries causing amplification, recommend they set Retry-After honor and use randomized exponential backoff. Also verify they're not reusing a short-lived token refill stamp across many workers (token refill rendezvous).

Alex: Will do. Customer asks for repro steps we can run internally — suggest I replay their sample with a 12-worker parallel curl loop hitting same token at minute boundaries. Any objections?

Anna: Sounds good. Use the test script with and without jitter to show difference. If we can reproduce, we'll attach the graphs to the ticket and schedule a short call with the customer.

Maria: I'll also check if any recent policy change tightened minute-window accounting. If we need, we can provision a targeted dedicated slot for them while they change their client.

Alex: Sending logs and sample script now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
